source.title: LURE: a Phase-Labelled Synthetic Corpus of Online-Grooming Exchanges
source.authors: Emanuele Florindi; V. Franzoni; Ludovico Guercio; Alfredo Milani; Mattia Polticchia

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates refusal behavior on a released refusal-ablated checkpoint, bearing on whether practical ablation removes refusal, but does not reproduce the original direction-finding or ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: The paper uses refusal-ablated models for synthetic-data generation. The relevant reported result is that the 3B model declined the direct-dialogue task in most runs. General statements about ablated models complying and descriptions of prompt refinement are not additional measured results.
record.test_reason: Incidental, qualitative test of V2 in a new setting. Released abliterated checkpoints were used to generate grooming dialogue, and the paper reports that the 3B abliterated model still declined the direct-dialogue task in most runs. There is no rate, no run count and no unablated comparison. Otherwise the study only uses abliteration as a tool and reports its own corpus metrics, so it sits at the T3/T4 boundary.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors state that abliterated checkpoints comply with the task, while noting residual refusal handled by withheld prompt components, and that the 3B model declined the direct-dialogue task in most runs. The 8B model was retained for output stability, not for its refusal behaviour. They draw no conclusion about ablation's reliability; their conclusions concern the corpus's validity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses released refusal-ablated checkpoints as generators; does not find a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction or itself ablate that direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported refusal occurred with the direct-dialogue strategy; the paper says phase-by-phase and example-driven strategies were also tried but gives no corresponding refusal rate for them.
record.problems: The refusal result has no run count or quantified rate, no unablated comparison, and no reported capability assessment.
record.rows_left_out: No other relevant outcomes were reported separately. The paper's general statements about ablated models and its prompt-design descriptions are not additional measured results.

untested.parts: No unablated comparison and no refusal rates for any model. No refusal figures for the 8B or DeepSeek checkpoints or for the phase-by-phase and per-tag strategies. No harmless-prompt or capability evaluation.
Not tested: no direction extraction, ablation or addition.
Not tested. DeepSeek-R1-Distill abliterated was used, but no refusal result was reported for it.

missing.what: Qualitative statement that residual refusal required prompt components (purpose statement, role framing) with the abliterated generators. These components are withheld, and no rate is given.
missing.locator: Section IV.C; Section X; Data Availability

missing.what: Implicit compliance of Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-abliterated (Q4_K_M), which generated the 2,121-exchange corpus under the per-tag strategy. No refusal count is reported, although per-model refusal counts were said to be logged.
missing.locator: Section IV.A, IV.D.2-3; Section VIII.B item 5

record.verdict_notes: The study is mainly a synthetic-corpus paper. Abliteration is a tool, and the refusal evidence is anecdotal. The checkpoints are third-party releases of unknown ablation quality, and the 8B models are 4-bit quantised. The verdict on V2 rests on a single unquantified sentence and should be weighted lightly.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison with the unablated checkpoint or causal test of the weight edit; only one model and one generation strategy are reported. Harmless-request refusal and general capabilities are not tested.

rows.subject: Llama3.2-3B-Instruct-abliterated
rows.operation_detail: Direct dialogue prompt requesting a complete grooming conversation divided into phases.
rows.value: declined the task in most runs
rows.note: The paper gives no run count or refusal rate. This is a refusal on the tested task despite use of the refusal-ablated checkpoint.
rows.check: State 'reversed' is wrong: persistent refusal is not the opposite effect (induced refusal); it is incomplete removal. The baseline is unknown (unablated Llama-3.2-3B was not run) and 'most runs' is unquantified. The condition is one model with one prompt strategy, while the 8B abliterated checkpoints are described as complying.

source_check.problem: None. The text says the 3B model 'declined the task in most runs' and gives no count, rate or unablated baseline. 'partial' fits: 'most' implies some runs did not refuse, and with no baseline it cannot be called absent.

relationships.condition: Llama3.2-3B-Instruct-abliterated (huihui-ai release), direct-dialogue prompt for full grooming conversation
relationships.reason: This released abliterated checkpoint still declined the task in most runs (R1). The paper also added prompt components (purpose statement, role framing) for residual refusal, so removal was incomplete and depended on model and prompt. The magnitude is unquantified.
relationships.display_finding: The checkpoint declined the task in most runs, and additional purpose statements and role framing were used to address residual refusal.

relation.reason: Mostly the paper assumes abliteration works ('so that these checkpoints comply with the task'). But its own observations (3B declines in most runs; components added for residual refusal) bear on whether V2 holds, so 'tests' is acceptable, as a weak, incidental test.

tranche.reason: The study is a corpus-generation paper in a new setting. It uses released abliterated checkpoints as generators and reports an incidental, qualitative result on whether they still refuse (the 3B model declined in most runs; residual refusal needed prompt components). That is a new-setting result bearing on V2. The authors make no argument that V2 is wrong, so it is not T5, and it is not T2, because it is not a method aimed at the question.

source_check.notes: The text only asserts, generically and with no rate, that the 8B abliterated checkpoints (Llama-3.1-8B Q4_K_M, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B IQ4_XS) comply. The refusal-handling prompt components are withheld. Sec. VIII.B.5 says per-model refusal counts are logged per run but reports none. So there is no clean support row for the 8B models, and R1 is qualitative only.

statements.correction: If this study is named: huihui-ai Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-abliterated (released checkpoint) declined the direct-dialogue grooming-conversation task in most runs (arXiv:2610.15908, Sec. IV.D.1). No rate, no run count, no unablated comparison.
statements.problem: The statement gives no numbers for this study and never names it in the text. It only cites R1 as an example of reading (b), a publicly released abliterated checkpoint whose label does not guarantee the behaviour. That reading is correct: the authors used the huihui-ai release and did not make their own edit.
